es.title: Noticias de Copyright e Inteligencia Artificial
es.subtitle: Notas publicadas por medios reales de la industria, con liga al artículo original. Sin noticias inventadas.

items.title: Italy’s competition watchdog probes Suno over ‘unfair terms’
items.summary: Suno’s legal headaches expanded beyond the US some time ago, with lawsuits filed by collecting societies in Europe and Scandinavia. Now Italy is getting in on the act – although this isn’t about copyright infringement. Well, not directly. The post is from Music Ally .

items.title: Japanese court says voice is protected by publicity rights; US appeals court says AI training is not fair use
items.summary: There have been two judgments this week of relevance to the ongoing AI debates in the music industry. A Japanese court ruled that publicity rights allow performers to stop unapproved AI voice clones. Meanwhile a US appeals court ruled against an AI company that used the good old fair use defence

items.title: Majors and BMG tell US Supreme Court not to let appeals court decision ‘radically disrupt copyright worldwide’ in songwriter termination rights case
items.summary: January 12 ruling held that termination under US law returns an author's rights across the world, and not only in the US Source

items.title: US appeals court rejects ‘fair use’ defense over AI training – as Thomson Reuters wins copyright case backed by RIAA and NMPA
Phono V streaming rate proposals filed with US Copyright Royalty Board, as DIMA points to 30% growth in publishing revenues since 2022
items.summary: The proceeding will set the mechanical rates on-demand streaming services pay US songwriters and publishers from 2028 through 2032. Source

items.title: AI Lost Its First Fair Use Appeal. Suno Should Be Worried.
Suno AI y GEMA: la batalla por los derechos de autor que puede redefinir el negocio de la música para la IA
Historic ruling on 'fair use' and AI may help Nashville songwriters
Trump’s DoJ was biased and wrong about ‘fair use’, say news orgs in OpenAI dispute
items.summary: Many of the music industry’s AI legal battles swing on whether or not AI training is ‘fair use’ under US copyright law. Donald Trump’s DoJ recently intervened in a dispute between newspapers and OpenAI insisting AI training is fair use. The newspapers have responded, explaining why the DoJ is wrong

items.title: Music-streaming fraudster Michael Smith gets 18-month jail sentence
items.summary: American producer Michael Smith has been sentenced to 18 months in prison for his infamous AI-powered streaming scam that netted him more than $8m in royalties. The post is from Music Ally .

items.title: Don’t say collusion: “no evidence of misconduct or conflict of interest” say major labels and publishers about their Phono V physical negotiations
items.summary: The US Copyright Royalty Board is reviewing what mechanical royalties songwriters and publishers should receive from 2028. It’s labels who pay mechanical royalties on physical records, and the major labels are keen to stress they aren’t colluding with the major publishers to keep the rates down

items.title: ARIA boss warns Australian politicians on AI lobbying demands
items.summary: Australia is one of the countries where the music industry is slugging it out with some tech companies to win the ears of politicians, as the latter mull what rules to put in place covering AI technology. The post is from Music Ally .

tip.title: Registra antes de publicar, no después
tip.body: El registro de tu obra no crea el derecho de autor —ese nace con la creación— pero sí te da la prueba con fecha cierta que vale en un juicio. Regístrala antes de subirla a plataformas, no cuando ya tengas el problema.

tip.title: Register before you release, not after
tip.body: Registration doesn't create your copyright —that exists from the moment of creation— but it gives you dated proof that holds up in court. Register before uploading to platforms, not after trouble shows up.
